To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PHC in children can be described by individual trajectories, (2) the course of PHC is different for self reports and parent reports, (3) the course of self reports is best described by increasing linear trajectories with significant individual differences, and (4) the course of parent reports is best described as a slowly increasing linear trajectory with significant individual differences.

the development of PHC is best described by an individual increasing linear trend that differs between children and adolescents, and that the development of these trends can be explained by mental health problems and other predictors.

psychosomatic health complains (PHC) of children and adolescents show individual trajectories that can be described by a linear trend, that the course of PHC differs significantly between individuals, and that mental health problems are the strongest predictors of PHC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of psychosomatic symptoms in children and adolescents and their predictors.
a comprehensive approach to psychosomatic health in childhood and adolescence and provides new insights into the development of PHC over time.

the identification of the best fitting function describing the individual trajectories of children and adolescents with PHC, the identification of differences in trajectories, and the prediction of these trajectories by known predictors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of PHC is not uniform but varies considerably between subjects and can only be described as an average trend.
the course of PHC in the general population of German children and adolescents is characterized by a slowly increasing level, but with significant inter-individual differences.
the individual development of PHC is not a simple and linear process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PHC are a rather stable phenomenon that increases slowly over time.
we have shown the development of PHC over time and that the individual course can be predicted by the level of mental health problems of children and adolescents.

the course of PHC is not uniform and that the individual development of PHC is associated with the mental health of the child or the adolescent, as well as with the mental health status of the parent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PHC are a dynamic construct and that the course is best explained by mental health problems.
the course of PHC in childhood and adolescence is not a linear increase over time, but rather a slowly increasing linear course with a decreasing slope.
the individual course of PHC can be described by different functions, which differ significantly between subjects, and which can be predicted by known risk factors.
